@Hyatt grew system-wide RevPAR by 7.2% in the third quarter of 2026, and its luxury hotels led the way.

The results, published on 29 October, show RevPAR up 8.2% in the United States, gross fees up 15.2% to $327 million and Adjusted EBITDA of $295 million.

The pipeline now holds about 158,000 rooms, up 12.1%. Openings in the quarter included Thompson Seville and Hyatt Vivid Punta Cana, the brand's first address in the Dominican Republic.

@Mark Hoplamazian, Chairman, President and CEO, linked the quarter to a growing preference for Hyatt's brands among guests, owners and developers. The group raised its full-year RevPAR outlook to 5.0–5.5%.

The one softer line: all-inclusive, where net package RevPAR slipped 2.5% on weaker demand in parts of Mexico.

The signal: at the big listed groups, luxury has become the engine of the quarter. For owners of high-end hotels, a raised outlook from the home of Park Hyatt and Alila is a good read on demand going into 2027.

Which luxury brand do you think is gaining the most ground right now?
